Що насправді означає lagom — слово, яке: What lagom really means – a word that explains a lot about the Swedish character. You read its story, work out where “in moderation” is appropriate, and together come up with tips for a newcomer: how to be lagom at work, in the neighbourhood or at a celebration.
Урок будується навколо одного слова: роз: The lesson is built around a single word: the “Är du lagom?” warm-up, the story of the word lagom, sorting situations, ranking the areas of life where “in moderation” matters most, and a group project. At home you write a text called “Hur lagom är du?”
Разом складаєте п’ять порад новачкові: я: Together you come up with five tips for a newcomer: how to be lagom at work, in the neighbourhood or at a Swedish party.
Чи прийнято розмовляти з незнайомцями в: Is it normal to talk to strangers on the bus – and which unwritten rules apply in Swedish public spaces? You learn to talk about rules with får, måste, behöver inte and brukar, and write a short scene about a small misunderstanding.
Спершу вгадуєш неписані правила, потім ч: First you guess the unwritten rules, then you read the text “Tyst på bussen?” and rank the rules from hardest to easiest for you. At the end you discuss the rules in your country, and at home you write a letter to a friend who is about to move to Sweden.
Модальні дієслова får, måste, behöver in: The modal verbs får, måste, behöver inte and brukar – for talking about rules and habits.
У групі пишете коротку сцену на шість ре: In a group you write a short six-line scene: on the bus, at work or when visiting someone, somebody unintentionally breaks a rule.
Fredagsmys — затишний п’ятничний вечір,: Fredagsmys – a cosy Friday evening that Swedes treat almost as a ritual. You read about this tradition, learn adverbs of frequency (alltid, ofta, ibland, sällan, aldrig) and plan the perfect Friday together.
Починаєш із власного п’ятничного вечора,: You start with your own Friday evening, sort things into “mysigt” and “not so much”, read the text “Dags för fredagsmys” and compare Swedish traditions with your own. At home you write a text called “Min perfekta fredag”.
Прислівники частоти alltid, ofta, ibland: The adverbs of frequency alltid, ofta, ibland, sällan, aldrig – for saying how often you do something.
У групі плануєте ідеальне fredagsmys: їж: In a group you plan the perfect fredagsmys: the food, the place, the activities – and how often you would do it.
Fika — це не просто кава з булочкою, а ш: Fika is not just coffee and a bun but a Swedish break for conversation and community. This lesson is shorter than the others: a text about fika, comprehension exercises, new words and a task where you put five fika-related things in order of importance and compare with a partner.
Короткий урок-знайомство з fika: розминк: A short introductory lesson on fika: the “Känner du igen dig?” warm-up, the text “Dags för fika”, a true-or-false exercise, new phrases and ranking five things connected with fika.
Розставляєш п’ять речей, пов’язаних із f: You rank five fika-related things by importance, then compare your ranking with a partner and explain the differences.
Чому шведи знімають взуття, коли заходят: Why Swedes take off their shoes when they go to someone’s home – and how to remind people of it politely. You practise reflexive pronouns (ta av sig skorna) and, in a group, design the perfect hallway of a Swedish home with a sign saying “Ta av er skorna!”
Починаєш із питання про власне взуття, в: You start with a question about your own shoes, guess the habits, read the text “Skor av, tack!” and talk about how things are done in your home. At home you write a text called “Min entré” about shoes in your own home.
Зворотні займенники (mig, dig, sig, oss): The reflexive pronouns (mig, dig, sig, oss) in the phrase ta av sig skorna – who exactly is taking their shoes off.
У групі проєктуєте ідеальний передпокій: In a group you design the perfect hallway of a Swedish home and write a sign, “Ta av er skorna!”, for guests.
Sambo, särbo чи gift — три способи жити: Sambo, särbo or gift – three ways of living together in Sweden. You read about each of them, learn to compare (vanligare, vanligast, bättre, bäst) and choose which option suits a fictional couple best.
Розминка «Hur vill du bo?», гра «Gissa n: The “Hur vill du bo?” warm-up, the “Gissa normen!” game about what counts as normal in Sweden, the text “Tre sätt att leva ihop” and a conversation about how couples live in your country.
Ступені порівняння прикметників: vanliga: Comparative and superlative adjectives: vanligare, vanligast, bättre, bäst – including the irregular ones.
У групі обираєте вигадану пару й вирішує: In a group you choose a fictional couple and decide what suits them best: sambo, gift or särbo.
Чому шведи так терпляче стоять у черзі —: Why Swedes queue so patiently – and how to describe who is standing where. You learn prepositions of place (framför, bakom, bredvid, mellan) and write a short scene in which someone jumps the queue.
Відповідаєш, як ти чекаєш у черзі, виріш: You say how you wait in a queue, decide what is “polite” in a queue and what isn’t, and read the text “Så väntar svenskar”. At home you write about a queue you remember.
Прийменники місця framför, bakom, bredvi: The prepositions of place framför, bakom, bredvid, mellan – for describing who is standing where.
Вигадуєте чотирьох-п’ятьох людей у черзі: You invent four or five people in a queue, describe who is standing where and write a short scene in which someone jumps the queue.
Jantelagen — неписані правила скромності: Jantelagen – the unwritten rules of modesty known from Sandemose’s novel. Do they still apply in modern Sweden? You read, learn abstract nouns ending in -het (jämlikhet, blygsamhet, trygghet) and, in groups, hold a debate for and against.
Розминка «Skryt eller blygsamhet?», пере: The “Skryt eller blygsamhet?” warm-up, a self-check against the “Jante rules”, the text “Du ska inte tro…” and a debate on whether these rules still apply. At home you share your own opinion in a text called “Min syn på jantelagen”.
Абстрактні іменники на -het: jämlikhet,: Abstract nouns ending in -het: jämlikhet, blygsamhet, frihet, trygghet – and how they are formed from adjectives.
У групах по четверо ділитеся на дві стор: In groups of four you split into two sides: one side argues that jantelagen still exists, the other that it is fading away.
Чому у Швеції не можна купити вино в суп: Why you can’t buy wine in a supermarket in Sweden – and why there is a state-run alcohol shop. You learn to talk about age (fylla 20 år, vara över 18) and make a poster or leaflet about Swedish alcohol rules for a friend who has just moved.
Урок про те, як у Швеції влаштований про: A lesson on how alcohol sales are organised in Sweden: a warm-up, the text “En butik med ensamrätt”, comprehension exercises and a comparison with habits in your country in the text “Alkohol här och där”.
Вік і межі: fylla X år, vara X år gammal: Age and limits: fylla X år, vara X år gammal, under / över X år.
Робите афішу або буклет про шведські пра: You make a poster or leaflet about Swedish alcohol rules for a friend who has just moved: age limits, what can be bought where and why such a system exists.
Allemansrätten — право гуляти, збирати я: Allemansrätten – the right to walk, pick berries and sleep in a tent almost anywhere in nature, but subject to certain rules. You learn prepositions of movement (genom, längs, in i, över, förbi) and draw a map of a walk, explaining what is allowed at each stop.
Сортуєш, що в природі дозволено, а що ні: You sort what is allowed in nature and what isn’t, read the text “Inte störa, inte förstöra” and compare Swedish walking rules with how things are in your country.
Прийменники руху й напрямку: genom, läng: Prepositions of movement and direction: genom, längs, in i, över, förbi.
Малюєте в групі просту карту прогулянки: In a group you draw a simple map of a walk with four or five stops and explain what is allowed at each one under allemansrätten.
Чотири маленькі слова, які змінюють тон: Four small words that change the tone of a whole sentence. You find out what ju, väl, nog and egentligen mean and learn to soften direct phrases so that you sound natural in Swedish – in a “before and after” exercise.
Розбираєш, чим розмовна мова відрізняєть: You look at how spoken language differs from written language, read the text “Fyra ord, en hel ton” and learn to sense how one small word changes the tone of a phrase. At home you soften your own sentences.
Модальні частки ju, väl, nog, egentligen: The modal particles ju, väl, nog, egentligen: what they mean and where they go in a sentence.
У парі переписуєте прямі речення з картк: In pairs you rewrite direct sentences from a card, adding ju, väl, nog or egentligen, and compare how the tone has changed.
Чому шведське «Vi får se» часто означає: Why the Swedish “Vi får se” often means “probably not” – and how to avoid going wrong when decoding evasive answers. You learn the construction det beror på + vad / om / hur / vem and find out what people really mean.
Сортуєш відповіді на прямі й ухильні, чи: You sort answers into direct and evasive, read the text “Nej utan att säga nej” and compare how people say no in Sweden and in your country.
Конструкція det beror på + vad / om / hu: The construction det beror på + vad / om / hur / vem – for answering questions depending on the circumstances.
У парі розшифровуєте ухильні відповіді н: In pairs you decode evasive answers such as “vi får se” or “det beror på”, working out what the person really meant.
«Det blir bra» — улюблена шведська заспо: “Det blir bra” – a favourite Swedish phrase for reassurance. You learn the difference between bli and vara (blir bra, blir kallt, blir svårt) and write a warm note to a friend who is worried.
Розминка «Vad tänker du?», гра «Orolig e: The warm-up “Vad tänker du?”, the game “Orolig eller lugn?”, the text “Ett svar man hör ofta” about why Swedes so often say “det blir bra”, and a conversation about how people reassure each other where you come from. At home you write what people in your country say to comfort someone and compare it with “det blir bra”.
bli чи vara: blir bra, blir kallt, blir: bli or vara: blir bra, blir kallt, blir svårt – a change of state versus a state that already exists.
Пишеш (сам або в парі) теплу записку дру: You write (on your own or with a partner) a warm note to a friend who is worried about an exam, a move or a job interview.
Asså, typ, liksom — слова-паразити, без: Asså, typ, liksom – the filler words that real spoken Swedish can’t do without. You work out when they sound natural, match them with their formal equivalents and write a dialogue that sounds authentic.
Дізнаєшся, коли asså, typ і liksom звуча: You find out when asså, typ and liksom sound unsure and when they’re simply natural, read the text “Ord som fyller tystnaden” and compare filler words in Swedish and in your language.
Розмовні слова та їхні формальні відпові: Colloquial words and their formal equivalents: asså / alltså ↔ så, typ ↔ ungefär, liksom ↔ på sätt och vis.
У парі пишете коротку природну розмову н: In pairs you write a short, natural conversation of six to eight lines in which at least four filler words sound right.
Orka! Palla! Lägg av! — вигуки й слова,: Orka! Palla! Lägg av! – exclamations and words that Swedes use every day and textbooks skip. You learn the imperative (Lägg av! Sluta! Kom igen!) and put together a quick guide to reactions for a new student.
Сортуєш реакції на позитивні й негативні: You sort reactions into positive and negative, read the text “Ord man faktiskt hör” and learn to understand words you hear in conversation but rarely see in a textbook. At home you describe the slang of your own language.
Наказовий спосіб: Lägg av! Sluta! Kom ig: The imperative: Lägg av! Sluta! Kom igen! Skärp dig! – and how it is formed from the infinitive.
У парі складаєте короткий довідник реакц: In pairs you put together a short guide to reactions for a new student: four or five everyday situations (tiredness, surprise, joy) and the most natural reaction for each.
Що насправді мають на увазі шведи, коли: What Swedes really mean when they say “intressant” or “inte dåligt”. You learn litotes – an understated expression that means more than it seems to – and write a polite but honest review of a mediocre film or restaurant.
Розрізняєш буквальний та іронічний зміст: You tell the literal meaning from the ironic one, read the text “Mer än orden säger” about the understated Swedish way of expressing things and compare how irony is understood in your language.
Літота: inte + прикметник як стримане тв: Litotes: inte + adjective as an understated statement (inte dåligt, inte direkt billigt).
Пишеш (сам або в парі) ввічливий, але че: You write (on your own or with a partner) a polite but honest review of a mediocre film or restaurant – no direct criticism, only litotes and things left unsaid.
Як чемно відмовити так, щоб тебе зрозумі: How to say no politely and still be understood. You learn polite refusal formulas (tyvärr, jag skulle gärna men…) and the construction hellre … än, and write a short, tactful message – declining an invitation or a request for help.
Відрізняєш чітку відмову від нечіткої, ч: You tell a clear refusal from a vague one, read the text “Ett tydligt nej, fast mjukt” and learn to say “no” gently but clearly. At home you write about how people say no where you come from.
Конструкція hellre … än («радше … ніж …»: The construction hellre … än (“rather … than …”) and the forms vill / skulle / ville – for declining and offering an alternative.
Пишеш коротке, чітке, але ввічливе повід: You write a short, clear but polite message declining an invitation, a request to help with a move, or a second date.
Чому шведи кажуть tack tack, hej hej, ja: Why Swedes say tack tack, hej hej, ja ja – and what each of these doublings means. You look at doubled words, get a feel for when they fit and put together a mini-dictionary with examples.
Вгадуєш, де шведи повторюють слово двічі: You guess where Swedes say a word twice, read the text “Två gånger är mer” and find out what doubling adds. At home you look for doubled words in your language.
Подвоєння слів: tack tack (більше вдячно: Doubled words: tack tack (extra gratitude), hej hej (a casual “bye-bye”), ja ja (reserved agreement), nej nej (reassurance).
У парі складаєте міні-словничок подвоєни: In pairs you put together a mini-dictionary of doubled words with an example for each and present it to the class.
П’ятнадцять буденних фраз, якими шведи п: Fifteen everyday phrases Swedes use to encourage and reassure people – from “det ordnar sig” to “ta det piano”. You learn reflexive verbs for things working themselves out (ordna sig, klara sig, reda sig, lösa sig) and create a game for matching phrases to situations.
Підбираєш фрази до ситуацій, де вони дор: You match phrases to the situations where they fit, read the text “Många sätt att säga samma sak” and collect fifteen everyday phrases of encouragement. At home you write about how people encourage each other in your language.
Зворотні дієслова самостійного розв’язан: Reflexive verbs for things working themselves out: ordna sig, klara sig, reda sig, lösa sig.
У парі робите гру: п’ять карток із фраза: In pairs you make a game: five cards with phrases (“det ordnar sig”, “ta det piano”) and five cards with situations, and another pair finds the matches.
Шведська, якої немає в підручниках: скор: Swedish that isn’t in the textbooks: abbreviations, reactions and colloquial words like oxå, iaf, najs. You learn how such abbreviations are formed and write a “coded” text message for another pair to decipher.
Вгадуєш значення скорочень і реакцій, чи: You guess the meaning of abbreviations and reactions, read the text “Det läroboken missar” about the Swedish that textbooks leave out and compare it with how words are shortened in your language.
Як утворюються скорочення: oxå, iaf, mkt: How abbreviations are formed: oxå, iaf, mkt, nml – and colloquial reactions like najs, lugnt, skönt.
У парі пишете SMS другові на три-чотири: In pairs you write a three- or four-sentence text message to a friend with abbreviations and reactions, and another pair decodes it into full sentences.
Чому ми відкладаємо справи, навіть коли: Why we put things off even when we know it will get worse. You read what researchers think about it, learn the future tense (ska, tänker, kommer att) and break a “scary” task into five small steps together.
Починаєш із впізнавання себе в ситуаціях: You start by recognising yourself in situations where you put things off, sort habits into those that help you get started and those that make you wait, and read the text “Plötsligt tvättar du”. At home you write a text called “Dags att börja”.
Майбутнє: ska та tänker (план) проти kom: The future: ska and tänker (a plan) versus kommer att (a prediction).
У групі беретеся за справу, яку часто ві: In a group you take on something that often gets put off (a letter, cleaning, a call to the doctor), break it into five small steps and set a time for each.
Інтроверт чи екстраверт — а може, трохи: Introvert or extrovert – or a bit of both? You learn the constructions både … och, antingen … eller and varken … eller, run a small survey in class and report the results.
Сортуєш ситуації за тим, що дає енергію,: You sort situations by what gives you energy and read the text “Lite av båda” about how most people are a bit introverted and a bit extroverted. At home you describe how you recharge in a text called “Så laddar jag batterierna”.
Парні сполучники både … och, antingen …: Paired conjunctions: både … och, antingen … eller, varken … eller.
У групі пишете п’ять запитань («Fest ell: In a group you write five questions (“Fest eller soffa?”), survey another group, count the answers and report the results to the class.
Чому ми порівнюємо себе з іншими — особл: Why we compare ourselves with others – especially on social media. You learn adjectives and verbs with fixed prepositions (stolt över, nöjd med, avundsjuk på) and look at what stays “behind the scenes” of the perfect post.
Сортуєш порівняння на «вгору» й «вниз»,: You sort comparisons into “upward” and “downward”, read the text “Den perfekta semesterbilden” and think about what doesn’t make it into the picture. At home you write a text called “När jag jämförde mig” about your own experience of comparing yourself with others.
Прикметники з постійними прийменниками:: Adjectives with fixed prepositions: stolt över, nöjd med, avundsjuk på, besviken på, jämföra sig med.
У групі вигадуєте чотири дописи в соцмер: In a group you invent four social media posts (a holiday, a gym selfie, a family dinner, a work update) and write what can be seen in them and what can’t.
Синдром самозванця: чому деякі люди почу: Impostor syndrome: why some people feel like frauds even when they’ve succeeded. You learn to talk about feelings and impressions (känna sig, kännas, verka, se ut) and write the script for a one-minute podcast episode on the topic.
Розрізняєш, що людина відчуває всередині: You distinguish between what a person feels inside and what shows on the outside, and read the text “Framgång eller bara tur?” about the feeling that you don’t belong. At home you write advice to a friend in a text called “Ett råd till en vän”.
känna sig, kännas, verka, se ut + прикме: känna sig, kännas, verka, se ut + adjective – for talking about feelings and impressions.
У парі чи трійкою пишете сценарій хвилин: In pairs or threes you write the script for a one-minute podcast episode about feeling like an impostor: a greeting, an example, a practical tip and an ending.
Чи можна навчитися бути щасливішим? Чита: Can you learn to be happier? You read what research says about it, learn the difference between perfekt and preteritum when reporting scientific findings, and write a “news story” about a made-up study – purely for practice.
Сортуєш радощі на швидкі й тривалі, чита: You sort joys into quick and lasting ones and read the text “Kan lycka tränas?” about what happiness research says. At home, in a text called “Något nytt att prova”, you choose something new to try.
perfekt чи preteritum: har visat проти d: perfekt or preteritum: har visat versus deltog – how to report research findings.
У групі вигадуєте невелике дослідження п: In a group you invent a small study about joy – purely for the exercise – and write a short news story: a headline, the participants, what the researchers did, the results and an expert’s tip.
Чому так важко змінити звичку — і що про: Why it’s so hard to change a habit – and what is actually known about it. You learn the construction det är svårt / lätt / viktigt att … and, in a group, play “myth or fact” about habits.
Відрізняєш звичку від свідомого вибору,: You tell a habit from a conscious choice, read the text “Mobilen bredvid kaffekoppen” and find out what research says about how habits form. At home, in a text called “Min nya vana”, you describe a new habit you want to build.
Конструкція det är + прикметник + att +: The construction det är + adjective + att + infinitive: det är svårt / lätt / viktigt att …
У групі пишете п’ять тверджень про звичк: In a group you write five statements about habits – some true, some myths – and swap them with another group, who decide whether each one is “myth or fact” and correct the myths.
Коли голова не вимикається: різниця між: When your mind won’t switch off: the difference between “fundera” and “älta”. You learn the construction sitta / ligga / stå / gå + och + verb (sitta och älta) and draw a “decision tree” for a thought going round in circles.
Сортуєш роздуми на «fundera» й «älta», ч: You sort thoughts into “fundera” and “älta” and read the text “Mitt i natten” about thoughts that keep you awake. At home you write about a thought that keeps going round in your head. The lesson ends with a gentle reminder to see a doctor or psychologist if it gets in the way of everyday life.
Псевдокоординація sitta / ligga / stå /: Pseudo-coordination with sitta / ligga / stå / gå + och + verb: sitta och älta, ligga och tänka.
У групі малюєте «дерево рішень» для думк: In a group you draw a “decision tree” for a thought that keeps going round in your head, starting with the question “Kan jag göra något åt det?”
Що нас мотивує: внутрішнє чи зовнішнє, «: What motivates us: from within or from outside, “lust eller lön”. You learn the constructions göra + adjective and få någon att + infinitive, and then present your own idea that helps people stay motivated – an app, a club or a challenge.
